attempted_claim: Let K be a number field and let Phi:A^2_K->A^2_K, Phi(x,y)=(f(x),g(y)), with f,g in K[x] disintegrated of degree >=2 (not linearly conjugate to x^d or +-C_d(x)). Let P in A^2(K) be non-preperiodic for Phi and let f:A^2->Y be a morphism to a quasi-projective Y/K presenting a flat algebraic family of curves C_y=f^{-1}(y). Assume no C_y contains a Phi-periodic positive-dimensional subvariety meeting the forward orbit O_Phi(P), so that |O_Phi(P) cap C_y|<infinity for every y in Y(K). Do there exist explicit K,Phi,P and f:X->Y as above for which sup_{y in Y(K)} |O_Phi(P) cap C_y| = +infinity, i.e. each fiber intersection is finite but their cardinalities are unbounded, with proof of both per-fiber finiteness and unboundedness? In particular exhibit one such tuple, e.g. with f(x,y)=x-y or another explicit pencil, if it exists.
decisive_failure: No explicit unbounded tuple was found and no uniform impossibility theorem was proved; the doubling/growth sketch toward uniformity was not closed to a place-uniform rigorous bound, and the grid computation covers only diagonal-pencil fibers over small disintegrated polynomials, so neither horn of the target is resolved.
